title: Feeding UVM with AnySource: retrieval methods, file structure and the fields to include

prose.text: AnySource is the generic connector for tools that have no dedicated vendor connector. {{connector-choice}}

prose.label: Retrieval.
prose.text: {{retrieval-methods}} The Upload File API's endpoint and format are not documented in any capture {{gap:upload-file-api}}. Creating the source otherwise follows [[aem.secops-platform:data-sources]].

prose.label: Other integrations.
prose.text: {{integration-count}} The connector list itself is not captured: [[aem.secops-platform:connector-catalog]].

checks.do: Whether every file uploaded to one AnySource source has the same structure (headers, file type) as the first; a different layout needs its own source.
Whether the file carries core identifiers (ID, name, first and last seen) so records correlate with other sources.

connector-choice.statement: A data source uses either a dedicated vendor connector or the AnySource connector; AnySource uploads files directly to the platform, stores them in their original format, and maps them to the platform's data model.

quotes: When creating a data source to ingest data into the platform, you can either use a dedicated vendor connector, or you can use the AnySource connector.
The AnySource connector allows you to upload files directly to the platform. Uploaded files are stored in their original format and can be mapped to the platform's data model.

retrieval-methods.statement: AnySource's file upload methods are Upload File, AWS S3, GCP, Webhook and Upload File API.

quotes: On the Create AnySource Source page, in the Retrieval section, select a file upload method:
- Upload File - AWS S3 - GCP - Webhook - Upload File API

consistent-structure.statement: Each source keeps a consistent field mapping, so all files uploaded to a source should match the structure of its original file, such as headers and file type.

quotes: Each source maintains a consistent field mapping, so all files uploaded to a given source should match the structure of the original file (e.g., headers, file type).

no-preprocessing.statement: The ingestion layer accepts a wide variety of file formats and structures, so preprocessing is generally not required.

quotes: The ingestion layer is designed to support a wide variety of file formats and structural variations, so preprocessing (e.g., data cleaning, reformatting) is generally not required

explicit-fields.statement: Unlike vendor connectors such as CrowdStrike Managed Hosts or ServiceNow Assets, AnySource needs the fields chosen explicitly: for a manual upload you can include them directly in the file, and field selection is typically handled through the parsing logic you define for the Upload File API; core identifiers (ID, name, first and last seen) support correlation across sources.

quotes: Unlike vendor-specific API connectors (e.g., CrowdStrike Managed Hosts, ServiceNow Assets), which automatically extract the necessary fields based on predefined integration logic, the AnySource connector requires you to explicitly determine which fields to include.
For example, when uploading a data file manually, you can choose to include the appropriate fields directly in the file.
In other cases, such as using the Upload File API, field selection is typically handled through the parsing logic you define.

Include core identifiers: Always export key attributes for each entity to support correlation across data sources (e.g., ID or unique key, name or title, and timestamps like first seen and last seen).

asset-fields.statement: Recommended asset fields are name or hostname, type, IP addresses, operating system, owner, location, status, tags, installed software and criticality.

quotes: | Asset Name/Hostname | The name or hostname of the asset |
| Asset Type | The type of asset (e.g., server, workstation) |
| External or Internal IP Address | The IP addresses associated with the asset |
| Operating System | The operating system running on the asset |
| Asset Owner | The individual or department responsible for the asset |
| Location | The physical or logical location of the asset |
| Asset Status | The status of the asset (e.g., active, decommissioned) |
| Asset Tags | The asset tags, if available.
| Software Installed | A list of installed software and software versions |
| Asset Criticality | The importance of the asset to the organization

finding-fields.statement: Recommended finding fields are vulnerability name or ID, severity (score and category), description, affected asset, CVE, threat intel, tags, first and last seen timestamps, recommendations, and affected component.

quotes: | Vulnerability Name/ID | The name or unique identifier for the vulnerability |
| Severity Score/CVSS/Scanner Score | The severity score assigned to the vulnerability, including the numerical score (8.1) and the category (High) |
| Description | A detailed description of the vulnerability and impact |
| Affected Asset | Information about the asset or system with the vulnerability |
| CVE | The CVE identifier, if available |
| Threat Intel Information | Threat intel parameters provided by the vendor |
| Tags | Vulnerability tags, if available.
| Timestamps | The First Seen and Last Seen fields
| Recommendations/Fix | Recommended actions for vulnerability remediation |
| Affected Component | Information about the affected component

integration-count.statement: Zscaler's UVM product page claims 150+ prebuilt integrations, an AnySource connector for flat files and webhooks, and an AnyTarget connector that pushes workflows, tickets and outputs to downstream systems.

quotes: **150+ prebuilt integrations**: native connectors for CVEs, threat intel, identity, applications, cloud services, user behavior
**AnySource connector**: integrate new data sources (flat files, webhooks)
**AnyTarget connector**: push workflows, tickets, outputs to any downstream system

upload-file-api.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the only source-backed API phrase is "Upload File API" as an AnySource ingestion method; no endpoint path, schema, auth scope or broader UVM administration API is captured or implemented in any vendored SDK, provider, MCP server or Postman collection.
